title: Everyday Greetings, Introductions & Farewells
description: Learn formal and informal greetings, asking how someone is, and polite farewells.
objectives: Greet people appropriately depending on the time of day and level of formality
Ask 'How are you?' and respond with polite conversational phrases

vocabularyList.definition: The period of time between midnight and noon, especially from sunrise to noon.
The time from noon or lunchtime to evening.
The period of time at the end of the day.
The period from sunset to sunrise in each twenty-four hours.
Of an extent, amount, or intensity considerably above normal; wonderful.
Used in polite requests or questions.

vocabularyList.exampleSentence: I am sorry for the delay.

sections.title: Greeting Conventions by Time of Day
sections.content:
In English, greetings vary depending on whether you are in a formal setting (e.g. at an interview, office, or university) or an informal setting (with friends or family).

Additionally, greetings change according to the **time of day**.

tables.title: Asking 'How are you?' & Polite Replies
rows: I am fine, thank you. And you?
آپ سے مل کر خوشی ہوئی۔

callouts.title: Never Greet with 'Good night'
callouts.text: 'Good night' is **only** used when leaving or going to bed, never when meeting someone in the evening! When arriving at 8:00 PM, always say **Good evening**.

callouts.title: Polite Return Question
callouts.text: When someone asks 'How are you?', it is customary to answer and then return the courtesy: 'I'm very well, thank you. **How about you?**'

exercises.prompt: You arrive at an office meeting at 7:00 PM. What is the correct greeting?
exercises.explanation: When arriving in the evening, say 'Good evening'. 'Good night' is only for departure or sleep.
exercises.urduExplanation: شام کے وقت پہنچنے پر 'Good evening' کہتے ہیں، 'Good night' صرف رخصت ہونے کے لیے ہے۔

exercises.prompt: Someone says: 'How do you do?' What is the traditional polite reply?
exercises.explanation: In formal English, the traditional reply to 'How do you do?' is 'How do you do?' or 'Pleasure to meet you.'
exercises.urduExplanation: رسمی تعارف میں 'How do you do?' کا روایتی جواب 'How do you do?' ہی ہوتا ہے۔

exercises.explanation: 'Nice to meet you' is standard polite social convention upon meeting someone.
exercises.urduExplanation: 'Nice to meet you' آپ سے مل کر خوشی ہوئی۔

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to form a polite farewell:
exercises.explanation: 'See you tomorrow afternoon' is a natural friendly farewell.
exercises.urduExplanation: کل دوپہر آپ سے ملاقات ہوگی۔

exercises.prompt: Match the greeting with the appropriate time of day:
exercises.explanation: Time of day dictates morning (AM), afternoon (early PM), and evening (late PM).
exercises.urduExplanation: وقت کے مطابق سلام کا انتخاب کریں۔

exercises.prompt: True or False: 'Good night' can be used to say hello to someone after dark.
exercises.explanation: False. 'Good night' is strictly a farewell.
exercises.urduExplanation: غلط۔ 'Good night' کبھی بھی سلام کے طور پر استعمال نہیں ہوتا، صرف رخصتی پر بولا جاتا ہے۔

exercises.prompt: Correct the greeting at 9:00 AM: 'Good afternoon, teacher.'
exercises.explanation: At 9:00 AM, the correct greeting is 'Good morning'.
exercises.urduExplanation: صبح 9 بجے 'Good morning' کہا جاتا ہے۔

exercises.prompt: I am fine, thank you. How _____ you?
exercises.explanation: 'How about you?' or 'How are you?' politely returns the inquiry.
exercises.urduExplanation: 'How about you?' آپ اپنے بارے میں بتائیے۔

exercises.explanation: 'My apologies' or 'Excuse me' expresses regret or polite apology.
exercises.urduExplanation: معذرت کے لیے 'Excuse me' یا 'My apologies' بولا جاتا ہے۔

exercises.explanation: 'Have a great weekend' is a typical Friday farewell.
exercises.urduExplanation: 'Have a great weekend' اچھا ویک اینڈ گزرے۔

exercises.prompt: Which greeting is used at 1:30 PM?
exercises.explanation: 1:30 PM is between 12:00 PM and evening, so 'Good afternoon' is correct.

exercises.prompt: When parting company at the end of the day, which phrase is appropriate?
exercises.explanation: 'Have a good evening!' is a polite farewell upon leaving.
exercises.urduExplanation: 'Have a good evening!' رخصت ہوتے وقت ایک شائستہ جملہ ہے۔

exercises.explanation: Days of the week take the preposition 'on': 'on Friday'.
exercises.urduExplanation: ہفتے کے دنوں کے ساتھ 'on' آتا ہے۔

exercises.prompt: What is the polite reply to 'Thank you very much'?
exercises.explanation: 'You're welcome' is the standard polite response to thanks.
exercises.urduExplanation: شکریے کا جواب 'You're welcome' دیا جاتا ہے۔

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct phrase for introducing yourself to a crowd:

options.text: My name is Bilal, and I am glad to meet everyone.
Me is Bilal, and I am here for the evening event.
I name Bilal, and I came from the downtown area.
Mine name is Bilal, and I want to say hello here.

exercises.explanation: 'My name is Bilal...' follows proper grammar and formal tone.
exercises.urduExplanation: اپنا تعارف کروانے کے لیے 'My name is...' درست طریقہ ہے۔

sections.title: اردو بولنے والوں کے لیے سماجی و لسانی رہنمائی
sections.urduText:
ہماری ثقافت میں دن کے ہر وقت 'السلام علیکم' کہا جاتا ہے، جو دن اور رات دونوں کے لیے موزوں ہے۔
انگریزی میں وقت کے لحاظ سے سلام بدلتا ہے: صبح 12 بجے تک **Good morning**، 12 سے 5 بجے تک **Good afternoon**، اور شام کے وقت **Good evening**۔
ایک عام غلطی یہ ہوتی ہے کہ لوگ رات کو کسی سے ملتے ہی 'Good night' کہہ دیتے ہیں۔ یاد رکھیں، Good night صرف الوداع (رخصتی) کے لیے بولا جاتا ہے!

sections.title: Lesson 4 Summary Box
summaryPoints: Use time-appropriate greetings: Good morning (AM), Good afternoon (12-5 PM), Good evening (PM).
Never say 'Good night' when arriving; reserve it exclusively for departure or bedtime.
When asked 'How are you?', answer politely ('I'm fine, thank you') and ask in return.
Standard farewells: Goodbye, See you tomorrow, Have a nice day.
